'''Stephon Haigh-Solomon Alexander''' is an American theoretical physicist, cosmologist, author, and jazz musician. He is a professor of physics at [[Brown University]] and works at the intersection of [[cosmology]], [[particle physics]], and [[quantum gravity]], with research involving string theory, [[loop quantum gravity]], gravitational parity violation, and the physics of the early universe.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://vivo.brown.edu/docs/s/salexan4_cv.pdf?dt=302110191 |title=Curriculum Vitae Stephon Haigh-Solomon Alexander |access-date=2023-04-12 |website=Brown University}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/radio/q/schedule-for-tuesday-april-26-2016-1.3553130/meet-the-physicist-who-brings-scientist-s-touch-to-jazz-1.3553135 |title=Meet the physicist who brings scientist's touch to jazz - Home {{pipe}} q {{pipe}} CBC Radio |publisher=Cbc.ca |date=2016-04-26 |accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Pesic |first=Peter |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/blue-notes-and-blackboards-1462562962 |title=Blue Notes and Blackboards |publisher=WSJ |date=2016-05-06 |accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://observer.com/2015/06/a-design-bible-focuses-in-on-physics-fast-food-and-meryl-streep/|title=A Design Bible Focuses in on Physics, Fast Food and Meryl Streep|website=[[The New York Observer]]|date=25 June 2015|publisher=|accessdate=12 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=cosmic_jazz_stephon_alexander |url=http://www.3rdspacecc.org/uploads/1/8/3/0/18304817/cosmic_jazz_stephon_alexander_2.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160919183340/http://www.3rdspacecc.org/uploads/1/8/3/0/18304817/cosmic_jazz_stephon_alexander_2.pdf |archive-date=2016-09-19 |access-date= |website= |publisher=}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Alexander was born in [[Trinidad]] and moved to the United States when he was eight. He grew up in the [[Bronx]], [[New York City]] and attended [[DeWitt Clinton High School]]<ref name=":0" /> where his physics teacher [[Daniel Kaplan (physicist)|Daniel Kaplan]] inspired him to study physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Jazz of Physics &#124; Stephon Alexander &#124; TEDxSanDiego |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v9_ZzY99-6U?t=178 |website=YouTube | date=3 December 2015 |publisher=TEDx Talks |accessdate=2015-12-03}}</ref>

He received a B.S. in physics from [[Haverford College]] in 1993 and subsequently studied at [[Brown University]], where he earned an Sc.M. in physics in 1995, an Sc.M. in electrical engineering in 1996, and a Ph.D. in physics in 2000. His doctoral adviser was [[Robert Brandenberger]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodman |first=Daniel |date=2019 |title=Find Your Path: Unconventional Lessons from 36 Leading Scientists and Engineers |url=https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262537544/find-your-path/ |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=MIT Press |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
After receiving his doctoral degree, Alexander was a research physicist at [[Imperial College]], London, as well as at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]], [[Stanford University]].<ref name="nytimes1">{{cite news|date=4 May 2016|title=Review: As Goes Music, So Goes the Universe|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/04/books/review-the-jazz-of-physics-by-stephon-alexander.html|accessdate=12 August 2016}}</ref> Alexander has held faculty positions at [[Penn State]], [[Haverford College]], and [[Dartmouth College]] before joining the faculty at Brown University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alexander, Stephon|url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/salexan4|access-date=2020-10-20|website=vivo.brown.edu}}</ref> Alexander was the president of the [[National Society of Black Physicists]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=President's Message|url=https://www.nsbp.org/nsbp-information/president-s-message|access-date=2020-10-27|website=www.nsbp.org}}</ref> He is also the executive director of Science and Arts Engagement New York Inc. (SAENY).<ref>{{Cite web|last=McCallister|first=Jared|title=CARIBBEAT: Trinidad-born physicist Stephon Alexander heads City College-backed program prepping young people for high-tech industry jobs|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/ny-caribbeat-stephon-alexander-physicist-cuny-tech-program-20200628-dkyix7omrjh5tnnw5rqhgqhmca-story.html|access-date=2020-10-27|website=nydailynews.com|date=28 June 2020 }}</ref>

===Academic life===
Alexander was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Imperial College London]] from 2000 to 2002 and subsequently at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] from 2002 to 2005. He joined [[Pennsylvania State University]] as an assistant professor of physics in 2005 and moved to [[Haverford College]] in 2008 as an associate professor. In 2012, he became the Ernest Everett 1907 Associate Professor of Natural Sciences at [[Dartmouth College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saker |first=Anne |date=2025-09-30 |title=Music and Science Unite in the Work of Cosmologist Stephon Alexander |url=https://skyandtelescope.org/astronomy-resources/famous-astronomers/music-and-science-unite-in-the-work-of-cosmologist-stephon-alexander/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=Sky & Telescope |language=en-US}}</ref>

Alexander returned to [[Brown University]] in 2016 as a professor of physics. He has also held visiting positions at [[Princeton University]], the [[California Institute of Technology]], [[ETH Zurich]], the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]], [[Columbia University]], and the Center for Computational Astrophysics of the Simons Foundation. Brown lists his current research specialization as the interface between cosmology, particle physics, and quantum gravity, including string theory and loop quantum gravity.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://www.stephonalexander.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/AlexanderCV-5.pdf|title=Academic life|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=|access-date=|archive-date=2017-04-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421195532/http://www.stephonalexander.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/AlexanderCV-5.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He has served on the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]]'' and has taught courses in general relativity and cosmology, astrophysics and cosmology, quantum field theory, and quantum mechanics. He also advocates for historically under-represented groups in the sciences.<ref name="nytimes1" /> He is a member of the [[editorial board]] of [[Universe (journal)|''Universe'']].<ref name="edbo">
{{Cite web
  | title =Editorial Board of ''Universe''
  | publisher =MDPI Publishing  
  | year =2016
  | url =http://www.mdpi.com/journal/universe/editors 
  | format =Online access 
  | doi = 
  | accessdate =2016-10-22}}</ref>

== Research ==
Alexander's research concerns fundamental questions at the intersection of [[cosmology]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Wheeler |first=Koby |date=2022-12-21 |title=Dr.Stephon Alexander: A Theoretical Physicist, Jazz Musician, and Author |url=https://sd2.org/stephon-alexander-a-theoretical-physicist-musician-and-author/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=San Diego Squared |language=en-US}}</ref> [[particle physics]] and [[gravity]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewton |first=Thomas |title=Stephon Alexander interview: Is the universe a self-learning AI? |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2289441-stephon-alexander-interview-is-the-universe-a-self-learning-ai/ |website=New Scientist}}</ref> His work has addressed the [[early universe]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=NOVA {{!}} Einstein's Big Idea {{!}} The Equation Today: Quantum Contemplations {{!}} PBS |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/einstein/toda-alexander.html |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.pbs.org}}</ref> [[cosmic inflation]], dark matter, [[dark energy]], [[black holes]], [[gravitational waves]], [[parity violation]], and possible extensions of general relativity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeLaCámara |first=Valerie |title=Stephon Alexander selected for the 2024 Frantz Fanon Award for Outstanding Achievements in Science, Philosophy and Leadership {{!}} Department of Physics {{!}} Brown University |url=https://physics.brown.edu/news/2024-01-26/stephon-alexander-wins-frantz-fanon-award |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=physics.brown.edu |language=en}}</ref>

=== String cosmology and inflation ===
One of Alexander's early research areas was [[string cosmology]], particularly the use of ideas from string theory to construct models of cosmic inflation. In a 2001 paper, ''Inflation from D-\bar{D} brane annihilation'', he proposed a scenario in which the annihilation of D5 and anti-D5 branes produces a vortex localized on a three-brane, with its false-vacuum energy driving an inflationary phase. The model also provided a mechanism for ending inflation and localizing matter on the resulting brane.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alexander |first=Stephon H. S. |date=2001 |title=Inflation from D-\bar{D} brane annihilation |journal=High Energy Physics - Theory |arxiv=hep-th/0105032 }}</ref>

His work in this area contributed to the development of models connecting higher-dimensional string theory with the dynamics of the early universe. Alexander is a co-inventor of a string-theory-based model of cosmic inflation developed in the early 2000s.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=February 21, 2022 - Dr. Stephon Alexander |url=https://nsbp.org/blogpost/1997746/449043/February-21-2022--Dr--Stephon-Alexander}}</ref>

=== Quantum gravity and parity violation ===
A recurring theme in Alexander's research has been the possibility that [[Quantum gravity|quantum-gravitational]] effects could produce observable departures from [[general relativity]]. His work has examined parity violation—the distinction between physical processes under spatial reflection and its possible consequences for cosmology and gravitational phenomena.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |title=The Cosmological Constant from a Quantum Gravitational $θ$-Vacua and the Gravitational Hall Effect |date=2025-06-17 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14886 |access-date=2026-10-11 |arxiv=2506.14886 |last2=Bernardo |first2=Heliudson |last3=Hui |first3=Aaron}}</ref>

In 2007, Alexander studied whether parity-violating modifications of general relativity could account for anomalies in the [[cosmic microwave background]], including suppression of power at large angular scales and possible alignments in the low multipole moments of the WMAP data. The work also considered connections between [[Parity (physics)|parity violation]] and [[leptogenesis]] in the [[Chronology of the universe|early universe]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alexander |first=Stephon H. S. |date=2008-03-06 |title=Is cosmic parity violation responsible for the anomalies in the WMAP data? |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269307015614 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=660 |issue=5 |pages=444–448 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2007.12.010 |arxiv=hep-th/0601034 |bibcode=2008PhLB..660..444A |issn=0370-2693}}</ref>

His later research developed these ideas through [[Chern–Simons theory|Chern–Simons]] modifications of gravity.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |last2=Yunes |first2=Nicolas |date=2009 |title=Chern-Simons Modified General Relativity |journal=Physics Reports |volume=480 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–55 |doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2009.07.002 |arxiv=0907.2562 |bibcode=2009PhR...480....1A }}</ref> In work beginning more than a decade ago, he developed what has been termed dynamical Chern–Simons gravity, an extension of [[general relativity]] involving a coupling between a [[scalar field]] and the gravitational Chern–Simons term. The theory provides a framework for investigating possible deviations from general relativity in strong-gravity environments and has applications to black holes, cosmology and gravitational waves.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |title=Fermionic cosmic strings in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity |date=2026-09-23 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28421 |access-date=2026-10-11 |arxiv=2609.28421 |last2=Bernardo |first2=Heliudson |last3=Zhang |first3=Shengyuan}}</ref>

Alexander has subsequently studied the propagation of gravitational waves in parity-violating theories. A 2020 paper examined [[gravitational waves]] in parity-violating Copernican universes,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |last2=Jenks |first2=Leah |last3=Jiroušek |first3=Pavel |last4=Magueijo |first4=João |last5=Złośnik |first5=Tom |date=2020-08-25 |title=Gravity waves in parity-violating Copernican Universes |journal=Physical Review D |volume=102 |issue=4 |article-number=044039 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.102.044039 |arxiv=2001.06373 |bibcode=2020PhRvD.102d4039A |issn=2470-0010}}</ref> while a 2024 ''Physical Review D'' paper with Tucker Manton investigated gravitational parity violation involving the [[Kalb–Ramond field]] and considered constraints from gravitational-wave observations, including [[GW170817]] and the GWTC-3 catalog.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Manton |first1=Tucker |last2=Alexander |first2=Stephon |date=2025-11-13 |title=Erratum: Kalb-Ramond field and gravitational parity violation [Phys. Rev. D 110 , 044067 (2024)] |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/fcs1-sdf7 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en |volume=112 |issue=10 |article-number=109902 |doi=10.1103/fcs1-sdf7 |bibcode=2025PhRvD.112j9902M |issn=2470-0010}}</ref>

=== Dark matter, dark energy and the early universe ===
Alexander's research has also addressed the nature of the [[Hidden sector|dark sector]], including theoretical approaches to [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |last2=Bernardo |first2=Heliudson |last3=Toomey |first3=Michael W. |date=2023-03-01 |title=Addressing the Hubble and Sub tensions with a kinetically mixed dark sector |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1475-7516/2023/03/037 |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |volume=2023 |issue=3 |pages=037 |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2023/03/037 |issn=1475-7516}}</ref> His work considers these problems in the context of the limitations of [[general relativity]] and the [[Standard Model]]. His research group has used theoretical, computational and conceptual methods, including machine learning, to investigate these questions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |last2=Cortês |first2=Marina |last3=Liddle |first3=Andrew R. |last4=Magueijo |first4=João |last5=Sims |first5=Robert |last6=Smolin |first6=Lee |date=2019-10-04 |title=Zero-parameter extension of general relativity with a varying cosmological constant |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.100.083506 |journal=Physical Review D |publisher=American Physical Society |volume=100 |issue=8 |article-number=083506 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.100.083506 |bibcode=2019PhRvD.100h3506A }}</ref>

He has also studied [[cosmic inflation]], [[leptogenesis]] and the generation of matter-antimatter asymmetry in the early universe. His research has examined how parity-violating interactions could produce an imbalance between matter and antimatter and how such effects might leave signatures in cosmological observations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon H. S. |last2=Peskin |first2=Michael E. |last3=Sheikh-Jabbari |first3=M. M. |date=2006 |title=Leptogenesis from Gravity Waves in Models of Inflation |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=96 |issue=8 |article-number=081301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.081301 |pmid=16606163 |arxiv=hep-th/0403069 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..96h1301A |issn=0031-9007}}</ref>

=== Gravitational waves and cosmology ===
Alexander has investigated whether observations of [[gravitational waves]] can provide evidence for physics beyond [[general relativity]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Stephon |last2=Daniel |first2=Tatsuya |last3=Manton |first3=Tucker |date=2026-07-01 |title=Beyond general relativity: gravitational waves in non-minimally coupled theories |journal=Physical Review D |volume=114 |issue=2 |pages=024005 |doi=10.1103/d8rf-d2wf |arxiv=2510.25895 |bibcode=2026PhRvD.114b4005A |issn=2470-0010}}</ref> His research examines how parity-violating interactions could affect the polarization and [[Gravitational waves|propagation of gravitational waves]] and whether these effects could be distinguished through astrophysical observations. His work with collaborators has considered constraints from existing gravitational-wave data and possible future tests.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yunes |first1=Nicolas |last2=O'Shaughnessy |first2=Richard |last3=Owen |first3=Benjamin J. |last4=Alexander |first4=Stephon |date=2010 |title=Testing gravitational parity violation with coincident gravitational waves and short gamma-ray bursts |journal=Phys. Rev. D 114 |volume=82 |issue=6 |article-number=064017 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.82.064017 |arxiv=1005.3310 |bibcode=2010PhRvD..82f4017Y }}</ref>

A 2021 [[Simons Foundation]] grant supported Alexander's research into modifications of general relativity, particularly approaches intended to address singularities associated with [[black holes]] and the [[Big Bang]]. The project examined whether an extension of [[Theory of relativity|Einstein's theory]] could provide a framework for understanding phenomena that remain unresolved within classical general relativity.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-30 |title=Grant will support gravity research that could update Einstein's theory of gravity {{!}} Brown University |url=https://www.brown.edu/news/2021-06-30/alexander |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=www.brown.edu |language=en}}</ref>

'''Interdisciplinary research'''

Alexander has also applied mathematical methods from theoretical physics to problems outside conventional cosmology. His research interests have included [[machine learning]], [[signal processing]], [[computational algorithms]], and mathematical approaches to musical perception. At Brown, he has participated in STEMJazz, an interdisciplinary initiative connecting science, mathematics, engineering and music.<ref>Stephon Alexander; Joao Magueijo; Antonino Marciano (June 2012). [https://inspirehep.net/record/1120119 "Hořava-Lifshitz theory as a Fermionic Aether in Ashtekar gravity"]. INSPIRE-HEP</ref><ref name=":2">Stephon Alexander; Antonino Marciano; Lee Smolin (December 2012). [https://inspirehep.net/record/1208288 "Gravitational origin of the weak interaction's chirality"]. INSPIRE-HEP.</ref><ref>Stephon Alexander; Martin Bojowald; Antonino Marciano; David Simpson (December 2012). [https://inspirehep.net/record/1206600 "Electric Time in Quantum Cosmology"]. INSPIRE-HEP.</ref><ref name="nytimes1" /><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/2016/05/chilling-brian-eno-changed-way-study-physics/|title=How Chilling With Brian Eno Changed the Way I Study Physics|date=2016-05-26|magazine=WIRED|author=Science|accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref>

=== Media ===
In February 2013, Alexander wrote in ''[[The New York Times]]'' about the need for black academics to set a positive trend for the next generation. In the article, he called upon a number of personal experiences from his own education and life.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/roomfordebate/2013/02/04/do-black-intellectuals-need-to-talk-about-race/black-academics-have-a-responsibility-to-the-next-generation "Black Academics Have a Responsibility to the Next Generation"]. NY Times. February 4, 2013.</ref>

Alexander has been interviewed or quoted in media sources such as the ''Tavis Smiley Show'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/wnet/tavissmiley/interviews/physicist-stephon-alexander/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160528063103/http://www.pbs.org/wnet/tavissmiley/interviews/physicist-stephon-alexander/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 28, 2016|title=Physicist Stephon Alexander {{!}} Interviews {{!}} Tavis Smiley|website=[[PBS]]|language=en-US|access-date=2016-08-31}}</ref> ''Forbes Magazine'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesinsights/2016/07/19/open-your-eyes-and-learn-from-others/#2cc0738732ef|title=Open Your Eyes And Learn From Others|last=Insights|first=Forbes|website=[[Forbes]]|access-date=2016-08-31}}</ref> ''NPR'',<ref>{{cite web|last1=Daniel |first1=Ari |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/codeswitch/2016/06/11/481664722/scientist-stephon-alexander-infinite-possibilities-unite-jazz-and-physics|title=Scientist Stephon Alexander: 'Infinite Possibilities' Unite Jazz And Physics|website=NPR.org|date=11 June 2016 |access-date=2016-08-31}}</ref> Brian Lehrer Show,<ref>{{Citation|title=Using Jazz to Explain the Multiverse|url=http://www.wnyc.org/story/physics-and-jazz/|accessdate=2016-08-31}}</ref> Science Salon/''Skeptic Society'',<ref>{{Citation|last=Skeptic Magazine|title=Dr. Stephon Alexander — The Jazz of Physics (Science Salon #6)|date=2016-06-20|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yOTfAcfX14M|accessdate=2016-08-31}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skeptic.com/past-lectures/jazz-of-physics-secret-link-between-music-and-structure-of-universe/|title=Dr. Stephon Alexander — The Jazz of Physics: The Secret Link Between Music and the Structure of the Universe (Science Salon # 6)|date=2016-05-22|language=en-US|access-date=2016-08-31}}</ref> ''Downbeat Magazine'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://downbeat.com/default.asp?sect=news&subsect=news_detail&nid=3271|title=DownBeat Magazine|website=downbeat.com|access-date=2016-08-31}}</ref> and ''Mercury News''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/peninsula-entertainment/ci_29882357/author-bridges-worlds-music-and-physics|title=Author bridges the worlds of music and physics|access-date=2016-08-31}}{{Dead link|date=January 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== Music ===
His album with [[Rioux (musician)|Rioux]]<ref name="factmag">{{cite web|author1=Fact |url=http://www.factmag.com/2014/07/17/premiere-stephon-alexander-and-rioux-recruit-no-wave-icon-arto-lindsay-for-ecstatic-i-guess-were-floating/|title=Premiere: Stephon Alexander and Rioux recruit No Wave icon Arto Lindsay for ecstatic 'I Guess We're Floating' – FACT Magazine: Music News, New Music.|work=Fact Magazine |publisher=factmag.com|accessdate=2014-09-13|date=2014-07-17}}</ref><ref name="djmag">{{cite web|url=http://www.djmag.ca/blog/2014/06/13/rioux-and-stephon-alexander-dance-illusion/|title=Rioux & Stephon Alexander – 'Dance of the Illusion' {{pipe}} DJ Mag Canada|access-date=2014-09-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701122624/http://www.djmag.ca/blog/2014/06/13/rioux-and-stephon-alexander-dance-illusion/|archive-date=2014-07-01}}</ref> was ''Here Comes Now''.<ref>{{cite web|author=SPIN |url=http://www.spin.com/2014/05/stephon-alexander-rioux-here-comes-now-stream-album/ |title=Hear Stephon Alexander & Rioux's Interstellar Jazz Excursion 'A Brief History Of Time' |publisher=SPIN |date=2014-05-29 |accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref> Alexander and bassist [[Melvin Gibbs]] formed a group that they named [[God Particle]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://bassmagazine.com/artists/melvin-gibbs-stephon-alexander-premiere-at-the-vision-festival-2019| date=May 14, 2019| title=Melvin Gibbs & Stephon Alexander Premiere at The Vision Festival 2019| newspaper=Bass Magazine - the Future of Bass| publisher=[[Bass Magazine]]| accessdate=2019-06-14}}</ref>  His first book, ''The Jazz of Physics: The Secret Link Between Music and the Structure of the Universe'', was published by Basic Books in 2016. The book examines historical and conceptual connections between music, mathematics and physics, including the work of figures such as Pythagoras, Johannes Kepler, Albert Einstein and John Coltrane.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Alexander |first=Stephon |url=http://archive.org/details/jazzofphysicssec0000alex |title=The jazz of physics : the secret link between music and the structure of the universe |date=2016 |publisher=New York : Basic Books, a member of Perseus Books Group |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-465-03499-4}}</ref>

His second book, ''Fear of a Black Universe: An Outsider's Guide to the Future of Physics'', was published by Basic Books in 2021. It discusses open problems in modern cosmology, including dark matter and dark energy, alongside Alexander's experiences as a physicist and his views on scientific creativity and diversity.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Alexander |first=Stephon |url=http://archive.org/details/fearofblackunive0000alex |title=Fear of a black universe : an outsider's guide to the future of physics |date=2021 |publisher=New York, NY : Basic Books, Hachette Book Group |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-1-5416-9963-2}}</ref>

Alexander is also the author of ''The Jazz of Physics'', a book that discusses the link between music and the structure of the universe.<ref name="autogenerated1" /><ref name="nytimes1" /><ref>{{cite web|last1=Levine |first1=Stuart R. |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesinsights/2016/07/19/open-your-eyes-and-learn-from-others/#6fe6eba232ef |title=Open Your Eyes And Learn From Others |work=Forbes.com |date= |accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Brooks |first=Michael |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2080677-bananas-and-jazz-help-us-penetrate-physics-but-only-so-far/ |title=Bananas and jazz help us penetrate physics – but only so far |publisher=New Scientist |date=2016-03-16 |accessdate=2016-08-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chron.com/neighborhood/bayarea/news/article/TCCHS-receives-engineering-certification-7288037.php|title=TCCHS receives engineering certification|publisher=|accessdate=12 August 2016|date=2016-04-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://kdhnews.com/harker_heights_herald/opinion/on_the_bookshelf/activity-packed-week-planned-at-harker-heights-public-library/article_c0d113e2-448c-11e6-a087-33a79dfb2f89.html|title=Activity-packed week planned at Harker Heights Public Library|date=8 July 2016 |publisher=|accessdate=12 August 2016}}</ref>

On a ''[[Nova (American TV series)|Nova]]'' documentary, Alexander was featured discussing his life as a jazz saxophonist, while also working as a physicist during the day.<ref name=":0">Marykwas, Donna (November 19, 2010). "PBS NOVA's secret life of scientist Stephon Alexander: sax-playing physicist".</ref>

==Other works==
Alexander founded Sound+Science, a nonprofit organization, and serves as its chief executive officer. The organization develops educational programs that combine music, science, and technology to introduce young people to STEM fields.<ref>{{cite web |title=Home - Official |url=http://soundplusscience.com/ |website=Sound + Science}}</ref>

He also founded and directs the Caribbean Future of Science project, established in 2023 with support from the Simons Foundation through the University of the West Indies. The initiative aims to connect Caribbean researchers, members of the scientific diaspora, and the international scientific community through regional scientific activities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Caribbean Futures of Science |url=https://www.planetaryself.com/caribbean-futures-of-science |website=Planetary Self}}</ref>
